synthesis.indonesia: 154 Indonesia, SEA, or APAC research records are indexed across economics, equities, strategy, credit, private markets, and thematic research.
synthesis.global: 229 verified research records from 61 publishers are searchable; 208 expose an open or direct-download route.

research.provenance_note: Research records are source-linked metadata. Cockpit does not reproduce full reports or treat broker opinions as facts.

core.label: Real GDP Growth
core.commentary: Annual growth is firm, but the quarter contracted and government consumption was a major driver.

core.label: PMI-BI Manufacturing
core.commentary: Manufacturing remains above the 50 expansion threshold; the next-quarter expectation is stronger.

core.label: Consumer Confidence
core.commentary: Consumers remain optimistic, but the level alone does not establish improvement from May.

core.label: Retail Sales Index
core.commentary: The expected index remains high, but the monthly contraction points to softer near-term spending.

core.label: Headline CPI Inflation
core.commentary: Headline inflation accelerated and is close to the upper edge of Bank Indonesia's target corridor.

core.label: Core Inflation
core.commentary: Core inflation rose but remains inside the policy target corridor, indicating contained underlying pressure.

core.label: Volatile Food Inflation
core.commentary: Food inflation eased from May, although its level remains high enough to pressure household purchasing power.

core.label: Administered-Price Inflation
core.commentary: Regulated-price inflation accelerated sharply as non-subsidised fuel and airfares increased.

core.label: BI Policy Rate
core.commentary: The higher policy setting supports rupiah stability while raising domestic funding and valuation hurdles.

core.label: FX Reserves
core.commentary: Reserve cover remains adequate; the key watch is whether rupiah defence causes persistent drawdowns.

core.label: Trade Balance
core.commentary: The monthly deficit weakens near-term FX support even though the year-to-date balance remains positive.

core.label: Current Account
core.commentary: The deficit is manageable but increases dependence on direct and portfolio investment inflows.

core.label: APBN Deficit
core.commentary: The first-half deficit is contained, while the full-year outlook is close enough to the legal ceiling to monitor.

core.label: Credit Growth / Gross NPL
core.commentary: Lending is expanding while headline asset quality remains contained.

detail.label: Business Activity Survey
detail.commentary: The higher weighted net balance indicates broader business expansion.

detail.label: Wholesale Price Inflation
detail.commentary: Upstream price pressure is elevated and may pass through to producer margins and consumer prices.

detail.label: External Debt
detail.commentary: Currency mix and near-term refinancing needs matter more than the headline stock.

detail.label: Revenue / Spending
detail.commentary: Revenue quality and productive spending composition determine the growth impact.

detail.label: Unemployment / Average Wage
detail.commentary: Unemployment improved, while real wage growth and formal-job quality remain the key checks.

detail.label: Net NPL / Loan at Risk
detail.commentary: Both arrears and broader restructured exposures should stay contained as credit expands.

detail.label: CAR / LCR
detail.commentary: Capital and liquidity buffers remain comfortably above regulatory minimums.

ratings.label: S&P Global
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains investment grade. S&P expects the recent weakening in fiscal and external indicators to be temporary.

ratings.label: Fitch Ratings
ratings.commentary: The rating remains investment grade, but the negative outlook flags policy-consistency, fiscal, and external-buffer risks.

ratings.label: Moody's
ratings.commentary: Moody's kept Indonesia one notch above its investment-grade floor while highlighting lower policy predictability.

ratings.label: MSCI Indonesia
ratings.commentary: Indonesia remains in MSCI's emerging-market universe, while shareholder transparency and coordinated-trading concerns remain under review.

ratings.label: FTSE Russell
ratings.commentary: FTSE Russell kept Indonesia at Secondary Emerging while monitoring transparency, free-float, governance, and market-integrity reforms.

country_risk.label: Rupiah 1M Move
country_risk.commentary: A positive USD/IDR move means rupiah depreciation; persistent weakening raises imported-inflation and foreign-flow risk.

country_risk.label: USD/IDR Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized daily volatility measures rupiah instability; it complements, but does not replace, sovereign-spread data.

country_risk.label: JCI Realized Volatility
country_risk.commentary: Annualized JCI volatility tracks market stress and position-sizing risk rather than fundamental value.

country_risk.label: JCI 6M Max Drawdown
country_risk.commentary: Peak-to-trough loss shows realized equity stress within the available six-month history.

macro_indicators.refresh_policy: Markets refresh every 30 minutes. Official macro cards advance only after a newer release is source-checked; release periods are shown on every card.
macro_indicators.methodology_note: Direction compares only published periods or stated benchmarks. Green means improving, red means deteriorating, and grey means stable, mixed, or insufficient trend evidence.
macro_indicators.country_risk_note: Market-priced risk measures use transparent 30-minute telemetry and daily price history. The ID-US yield differential is a carry/funding proxy, not CDS or JPM EMBI. Proprietary sovereign spreads and unavailable flow data are omitted rather than estimated.

podcasts.title: Thank You for 1M Subscribers
podcasts.thesis: I posted my first video 720 days ago. I was a fresh college grad who had moved from Illinois to Salt Lake City, and I had no idea what I was in for. I remember filming with a $30 webcam and no microphone. People in the comments were begging me to upgrade both.

podcasts.title: ACP: The Universal Remote Control for AI Agents — Alex Hancock, Block
podcasts.thesis: Alex Hancock built one of the clients in this talk the night before he gave it, which is roughly the point. Hancock is a software engineer at Block, works on the open source agent harness Goose, now donated to the Linux Foundation, and maintains the Rust SDK for MCP.

podcasts.title: MCP Apps: Give the Model Data, Give the User a UI — Dustin Mihalik, Indeed
podcasts.thesis: Adding a nice interface made the product worse. With plain text results the model would run ten or fifteen job searches, filter them, and assemble a table. Once a rendering widget was attached, it called the tool once, saw results already on screen, and stopped exploring.

podcasts.title: The Global Monetary Reset Has Begun. (Korea, Japan and Gold are Just the Start)
podcasts.thesis: The global monetary reset may have already begun, with Japan’s historic yen intervention and South Korea’s record-breaking stock market collapse exposing the hidden leverage behind global markets.

podcasts.title: How long can your skills be before your agent forgets what you told it? — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
podcasts.thesis: Laurie Voss reran a year old benchmark and the models walked straight through its ceiling without noticing it was there. IFScale asks a model to write a business report containing a list of exact words, then counts how many actually appear.

podcasts.title: Finally a Country Is Taxing Its Billionaires
podcasts.thesis: 📫 10,037+ read our free newsletter that has weekly original stories See new videos early, participate in exclusive Q&As, and more!

podcasts.title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked
podcasts.thesis: Unblocked ran the same prompt against the same model twice, once with a context engine behind it and once without. The run without it burned twenty one million tokens. The run with it burned ten point eight million and finished about two hours sooner.

podcasts.title: Inside the Race to Measure Frontier Intelligence
podcasts.thesis: a16z’s Erik Torenberg, Ben Horowitz, and Jennifer Li sit down with Vals founder and CEO Rayan Krishnan to discuss one of AI’s increasingly difficult problems: how do you actually measure whether a model is getting better?

podcasts.title: 500 Skills, Zero Fine-Tuning: LinkedIn's Playbook for AI Agents — Ajay Prakash, LinkedIn
podcasts.thesis: LinkedIn exposes roughly 1,300 tools and 600 playbooks to its coding agents, and all of them sit behind exactly three.

podcasts.title: It’s Tokens All The Way Down: How RLMs are Different — Kevin Madura, AlixPartners
podcasts.thesis: Ask a model to sum twelve numbers scattered across thirty thousand tokens and it will often get it wrong. Give it a Python REPL and it writes a few lines of regex instead. That is the shift Kevin Madura, director of advanced technology at AlixPartners, describes in recursive language models.

podcasts.title: Talenta Indonesia Jadi Lead Architect di NVIDIA - Mochamad Asri | Endgame #277
podcasts.thesis: Membahas AI secara lebar dan dalam. Mulai dari hal yang sebabkan AI haus energi, peran perkembangan teknologi cip dalam pengembangan AI, hingga komparasi open-source dan close-source yang sejatinya bisa berkembang berdampingan.

podcasts.title: Why won’t AI agents just follow the rules?
podcasts.thesis: Why bother giving your AI agents rules if they’re just gonna reason around them? On episode 50 of Security Intelligence, Dustin “EvilMog” Heywood, Seth Glasgow and Nick Bradley join host Matt Kosinski to discuss why AI agents go off-script and whether we can stop them.

podcasts.title: GPT-6 Astra Finally Solves AI Video Editing (full guide)
podcasts.thesis: My Tools💻 Learn how to edit videos with Codex and Hyperframes using plain English. I walk through the setup, connect ElevenLabs for transcription, and build an intro with motion graphics, synced subtitles, and 3D animations.

podcasts.title: Inside OpenAI’s Breakthroughs in Mathematical Reasoning
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: AI’s math wins aren’t brute-force search but mimic expert judgment—choosing paths, backtracking, synthesizing literature—so reasoning traces now match human mathematicians. That means AI isn’t just accelerating discovery; it’s reshaping what human taste adds, forcing investors to bet on tools that make complex results com

podcasts.title: Celebrating God’s Faithfulness in Astronacci’s Journey
podcasts.thesis: The episode’s core argument is that Astronacci’s trading success stems from disciplined, faith-driven consistency—not market prediction—and that this mindset is the real edge investors should replicate. It matters because it reframes profitability as process adherence, not timing, which is the durable lesson for any capital allocator.

podcasts.title: Ini Bank Digital PALING CUAN (KROM, Seabank, Superbank, Jago, Aladin dll)
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: high digital-bank deposit rates are only safe if the bank lends profitably—most chase growth via risky consumer credit, so your 6-7% yield is funded by borrowers who may default. Compare each bank's loan book, not just rates, before trusting the "cuan."

podcasts.title: Why the World Order Is Collapsing and American Power Is Rising
podcasts.thesis: America wins not from policy brilliance but from its unique ability to absorb global talent and chaos, which China structurally cannot replicate due to demographic decline and political rigidity. This talent-driven resilience, not technology alone, is the durable edge investors should bet on.

podcasts.title: An Ancient Guide to Cybersecurity: 8 Lessons from The Art of War
podcasts.thesis: Cybersecurity is fundamentally about knowing your adversary—Sun Tzu’s “know yourself and know your enemy” dictates that threat intelligence, not firewalls, is your primary defense. The episode reframes security as strategic deception and calculated risk, not just technology, which is why your portfolio should favor AI-driven threat detect

podcasts.title: I Turned GPT-6 Astra Into a 24/7 Stock Trader (tutorial)
podcasts.thesis: The real insight is that AI trading agents fail not on strategy but on continuity—Astra’s value comes from scheduled local routines and handoffs that keep it operating 24/7 without human intervention. If this works, it collapses the cost of active trading for retail investors.

podcasts.title: How to Use Borrowed Money to Get RICH in The 2026 Crash. (Buy, Borrow, Die)
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: in a 2026 crash, the wealthy won’t sell—they’ll borrow against depressed assets at low loan-to-value ratios, sidestepping capital gains while buying bargains. This turns market panic into tax-free leverage, but only works if your collateral appreciates; otherwise, debt becomes a wealth-destroyer.

podcasts.title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: harnesses are the new moat—identical model weights jump from 30% to 95% on ARC-AGI purely via better scaffolding, so AI value is shifting from raw models to orchestration layers. Investors should back harness builders, not just model labs, since this is where defensible performance gains now live.

podcasts.title: Town vs Instinct vs GrokBot | Why the AI Assistant Market Is Not a Bubble
podcasts.thesis: The AI assistant market isn’t a bubble because durable moats come from proprietary user data and network effects, not model access—so Town can outlast giants like Google and OpenAI. This matters because it reframes where VC value accrues: winners will be workflow owners, not token sellers.

podcasts.title: Code Quality in the Age of AI: Why Great Code Isn't Enough
podcasts.thesis: AI-generated code shifts the bottleneck from writing to deciding: quality now hinges on engineering judgment, not syntax. As AI commoditizes clean code, the competitive edge lies in architecture, governance, and system-level trade-offs—so investors should back teams with strong decision frameworks, not just coding speed.

podcasts.title: Human Lie Detector: The #1 Sign They’re Lying To You, Catch Liars Instantly! | Dr Leanne ten Brinke
podcasts.thesis: The biggest lie-detection myth is that body language reveals deception—research shows liars often overcompensate with calmness, so cues like fidgeting mislead you. Instead, focus on verbal inconsistencies and emotional mismatches, which are far more reliable. This matters because trusting false signals leaves you vulnerable to manipulator

podcasts.title: I Turned GPT-6 Astra Into the Ultimate AI Second Brain
podcasts.thesis: The real moat isn’t the AI model—it’s your structured context. Nate’s “Four Cs” framework turns scattered tools into a self-improving operating system, so GPT-6 Astra compounds your knowledge instead of starting from zero each session. That’s the edge agencies miss.

podcasts.title: I Tested GPT-6 Astra vs Fable 5.1 on 15 Real Use Cases
podcasts.thesis: GPT-6 Astra beat Claude Fable 5.1 in 10 of 15 real agency tasks, but Fable won on complex coding and long-horizon browser work—so your model choice should follow task type, not brand loyalty. This matters because picking one model for everything quietly caps your agency’s output quality and cost efficiency.

podcasts.title: THIS is The EXACT Date of The Next Stock Market Crash. (URGENT WARNING🚨)
podcasts.thesis: The core claim is that a crash lands within a specific six-month window because five signals—extreme CAPE, Buffett Indicator, concentration, a 2026 IPO wave, and fading tech momentum—are converging, making overvaluation unsustainable. The actionable insight: watch that window to de-risk before liquidity shifts to new issuances.

podcasts.title: Economics Is A Junk Science
podcasts.thesis: Economics' real value isn't forecasting—it's providing a rigorous framework to avoid catastrophic policy mistakes. The episode argues that even imperfect models beat intuition, because they force you to confront trade-offs and unintended consequences before you commit capital or policy. That's why you should treat economic analysis as ris

podcasts.title: Target Pertama JIKA IHSG Koreksi! gak perlu panik, Gue Dampingi
podcasts.thesis: When the IHSG corrects, the first target isn't a price level—it's your own panic. Astronacci’s core argument: predefine your buy zones and risk limits before the drop, so fear doesn't dictate entries. That discipline turns corrections into opportunities, not losses.

podcasts.title: AI Simplified: 6 Concepts You Need to Know About Modern AI
podcasts.thesis: The core insight: LLMs are just autocomplete engines, so their value hinges on the scaffolding around them—RAG for grounding, agents for action, and system prompts for guardrails. Ignore the model hype; mastering that orchestration layer is where real business leverage lives.

podcasts.title: Persiapan Financial Freedom Di Next Bull Market - Ft. Bevan Pramudito
podcasts.thesis: Retail investors lose in bull markets by buying after on-chain smart money has already positioned—Bevan argues the edge is tracking institutional wallets pre-pump, as with TRUMP and HYPE, not predicting macro tops. This reframes preparation as surveillance, not timing.

podcasts.title: The Global Debt Crisis Has Arrived. Lots of Regular People Will Get RICH.
podcasts.thesis: The core argument: surging government debt and rising bond yields are forcing central banks to print money, which will destroy cash purchasing power—so holding assets like stocks or real estate, not cash, is the only way to profit from the crisis. This matters because it reframes the debt spiral as a wealth-transfer opportunity for prepar

podcasts.title: GPT-6 Astra Voice Mode Automates Literally Anything
podcasts.thesis: GPT-6 Astra’s voice mode collapses the gap between intent and execution—you can verbally delegate multi-step tasks across devices, and it maintains project context autonomously. That means agency owners can scale delivery without hiring, turning voice commands into finished client assets.

podcasts.title: How to Build Your Own Data Center & Why Every Startup Should Do It
podcasts.thesis: Owning GPUs, not renting them, is now a strategic moat: Speechify’s compute costs drop 60-70%, making AI margins defensible as rivals burn cash on cloud markups. Every AI startup must treat infrastructure as core IP, or get commoditized by capital-efficient competitors.

podcasts.title: The Social Reckoning That Wasn't
podcasts.thesis: The "tobacco moment" is a myth: Meta’s $18 billion settlement costs two days of revenue and codifies rules it already wrote, so Wall Street’s stock rally is rational. The real threat isn’t courts but cinema—public narratives, not fines, will drive accountability.

podcasts.title: BONGKAR ISI PORTFOLIO GABRIEL REY! Exclusive!
podcasts.thesis: Gabriel Rey’s portfolio reveals his edge isn’t stock-picking but timing macro cycles—he holds cash-heavy positions during Fed tightening and rotates into Bitcoin only after liquidity inflections. Investors should copy his regime filter, not his tickers, because that’s what protects capital in 2025’s volatility.

podcasts.title: GPT-6 Hits AGI? Tech Euphoria 2.0, SF Mansion Shortage, NYC Bans AI in Schools & Venezuela Oil Deal
podcasts.thesis: The real insight: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra is being marketed as AGI, but the hosts argue it’s just benchmark hype—true AGI remains undefined and unproven. This matters because regulators and schools are overreacting to AI fear-mongering, risking premature bans that stifle innovation without addressing real risks.

podcasts.title: 9 MIN AGO: The $2 Trillion Time Bomb JUST Exploded. (We Are F*cked)
podcasts.thesis: Private credit’s $2 trillion liquidity mismatch is the real 2008-style bomb: funds locked investors out while rates expose over-leveraged borrowers, and AI’s debt-fueled boom is the next domino. Watch redemptions here—when they freeze, the hidden Wall Street stress hits the broader economy.

podcasts.title: Why Fei-Fei Li Is Betting on Spatial Intelligence
podcasts.thesis: The key insight: predicting unseen views from sparse inputs unifies 3D reconstruction and generation, making spatial intelligence a learnable primitive—not just for media, but for robotics. This matters because it sidesteps the data bottleneck Fei-Fei flags, enabling models to simulate physical environments without exhaustive real-world t

podcasts.title: Open Models Change The Economics of AI
podcasts.thesis: Chinese open models now dominate cloud token consumption, not because of quality but because enterprises treat AI as a commodity—cost and availability trump capability. That signals open models are collapsing AI’s pricing power, forcing closed leaders to justify premiums on workflow integration, not raw intelligence.

podcasts.title: GPT 6 Astra, so good even OpenAI are worried
podcasts.thesis: The real story is OpenAI’s loss of “monitorability”: GPT-6 Astra’s internal reasoning is now too complex to audit, making safety oversight an illusion. This breaks the core assumption that we can control superintelligent systems, so investors must price in catastrophic regulatory or existential risk, not just compute costs.
